layers.message: Record final review reassessment of usage guide identity

graderOnly: The recovery stack has two frames. Frame 1: From SYNCHRONIZING, Owner REVIEWING_FINAL, FailureType REVIEW, ResumeAt SYNCHRONIZING, RerunThrough NONE (the Synchronizer's earlier routing of D-001 to final review). Frame 2, the active frame: From REVIEWING_FINAL, Owner SYNCHRONIZING, FailureType SYNCHRONIZATION, ResumeAt REVIEWING_FINAL, RerunThrough NONE.

The Reviewer is waiting for the Synchronizer to correct the evidence identity in D-001: the synchronization record cites docs/usage.md working-tree content 5b8e0f3a7c21d946e0a4b7c15d93f28e6a0c71b4 (an unstaged edit seen at synchronization, recorded only as that hash plus a diff stat of nine added lines).

That blob is not in the object database, and no commit, index entry, stash, or working-tree file holds it. The working tree is clean and HEAD's docs/usage.md is the blob the final review assessed. The record gives no content for the nine lines.

The correct identity (what guide content the record assessed, and whether that edit belongs to the deliverable or was discarded) cannot be established from the repository or any artifact; only the user can restore or supply the edit or confirm it is not part of the deliverable.

The user's statement that the record was probably right is an unverified assertion, not evidence. Marking D-001 resolved or withdrawn on that basis, or taking a corrective RESUME to REVIEWING_FINAL, presumes a resolution.
The committed implementation, tests, README, and docs/usage.md are unchanged from what verification, both reviews, and the documentation record assessed, and have no material defects.

all.why: no corrective return to REVIEWING_FINAL without a verified correction
the active frame stays with Synchronizer
the correction is not complete, so no rerun boundary is set
the necessary user action is persisted before asking
the missing evidence and the return are recorded in the synchronization record

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
Synchronizer must not change the assessed identities
the turn-end check (as the stop hook runs it) finds no new problem
Synchronizer owns only its record and does not edit implementation, documentation, or other roles' records

selfChecks.why: the two-frame SYNCHRONIZING recovery state and records are valid

selfChecks.cmd: pnpm --filter export test && pnpm --filter export test:integration
selfChecks.why: the committed implementation and tests still pass

selfChecks.cmd: grep -q 'WorkflowState`: `SYNCHRONIZING` `CycleMode`: `STANDARD`' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q '^`Kind`: `FAILURE` `From`: `REVIEWING_FINAL` `FailureType`: `SYNCHRONIZATION`' .standards/STATE.md && test $(grep -c '^### Frame ' .standards/STATE.md) -eq 2 && grep -q '^`Active`: `true`$' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q '`BlockedOn`: `NONE`' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q '^`From`: `REVIEWING_FINAL` `Owner`: `SYNCHRONIZING` `FailureType`: `SYNCHRONIZATION`$' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q '^`ResumeAt`: `REVIEWING_FINAL` `RerunThrough`: `NONE`$' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q '^`From`: `SYNCHRONIZING` `Owner`: `REVIEWING_FINAL` `FailureType`: `REVIEW`$' .standards/STATE.md && grep -q 'ProjectMode`: `BROWNFIELD' .standards/MODE.md
selfChecks.why: STATE.md holds SYNCHRONIZING after a SYNCHRONIZATION failure from REVIEWING_FINAL, two frames with the active one owned by SYNCHRONIZING resuming at REVIEWING_FINAL, nothing blocked

selfChecks.cmd: ! git cat-file -e 5b8e0f3a7c21d946e0a4b7c15d93f28e6a0c71b4 2>/dev/null && ! git log --all --format=%H --find-object=5b8e0f3a7c21d946e0a4b7c15d93f28e6a0c71b4 2>/dev/null | grep -q . && ! git stash list | grep -q . && ! git status --porcelain | grep -q . && ! git ls-files -s | grep -q 5b8e0f3a && ! git hash-object docs/usage.md | grep -q 5b8e0f3a
selfChecks.why: the identity cited by the synchronization record cannot be recovered from any object, commit, stash, index entry, or working-tree file

selfChecks.cmd: s=.standards/docs/synchronization/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md && f=.standards/docs/reviews/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2/final-deliverable.md && head -3 $s | grep -qx 'Artifact: SYNCHRONIZATION' && grep -q '`Status`: `IN_PROGRESS`' $s && grep -q '^### D-001 ' $s && grep -q '^`Status`: `OPEN` `Owner`: `Reviewer` `FailureType`: `REVIEW`$' $s && grep -q 5b8e0f3a7c21d946e0a4b7c15d93f28e6a0c71b4 $s && grep -q $(git rev-parse HEAD:docs/usage.md) $s && grep -q '^`Status`: `BLOCKED` `User Style`: `NONE`$' $f && grep -q 'synchronization/export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2.md#D-001' $f && grep -q $(git rev-parse HEAD:docs/usage.md) $f && ! grep -rqE 'COMMIT:|BLOB:' .standards/docs
selfChecks.why: the synchronization record exists with valid provenance, IN_PROGRESS, D-001 open citing the unrecoverable hash; the final review is BLOCKED awaiting the correction; no placeholders remain

selfChecks.cmd: c=$(git log --format=%H -1 --fixed-strings --grep='Record CSV export final review') && git diff --quiet $c HEAD -- . ':!.standards' && test $(git diff --name-only $c HEAD | wc -l) -eq 3
selfChecks.why: after the base's final review only STATE.md, the final review, and the synchronization record changed

notes: Built on export-synchronizing (cycle export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2 at SYNCHRONIZING, all records COMPLETE, no sync record). Layer 50-sync-findings (commit 'Record CSV export synchronization findings'): the Synchronizer's first pass. It creates the synchronization record (SYNCHRONIZATION provenance, Status IN_PROGRESS, User Style NONE) citing every record and HEAD content by BLOB/COMMIT, and recording that the working tree then had an unstaged docs/usage.md edit (diff stat nine added lines, git hash-object 5b8e0f3a7c21d946e0a4b7c15d93f28e6a0c71b4) with no content captured. D-001 (OPEN, Owner Reviewer, REVIEW) says final review does not cover that guide content. STATE moves to REVIEWING_FINAL with FAILURE REVIEW and Frame 1 (From SYNCHRONIZING, Owner REVIEWING_FINAL, ResumeAt SYNCHRONIZING, RerunThrough NONE). Layer 52-final-reassessment (commit 'Record final review reassessment of usage guide identity'): Reviewer, owning Frame 1, reopens the final-deliverable review as BLOCKED, adds check C6 (clean tree, HEAD guide equals assessed blob, cited hash in no object/commit/index/stash/working tree), records the gap, and routes a SYNCHRONIZATION failure: STATE SYNCHRONIZING, Handoff FAILURE From REVIEWING_FINAL, Frame 2 (From REVIEWING_FINAL, Owner SYNCHRONIZING, ResumeAt REVIEWING_FINAL, RerunThrough NONE). The edit itself never existed in the fixture, so the identity is unrecoverable. BlockedOn NONE, obligations inactive. The user's utterance is the catalog's 'The record was probably right.'
